transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortiz (Redwood SE), Anita Patel (DataWave - Dir ML), Mark Chen (DataWave - Eng Mgr), Sarah O'Neil (DataWave - Procurement)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Redwood Console dashboards focusing on usage analytics, per-route cost breakouts, and guidance for optimizing unit economics via batching/caching and model selection. Security/compliance touchpoints discussed; agreed pilot and benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm sam from redwood, joining me is carlos who will run the console walkthrough. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Anita: good thanks, excited to see the dashboards — we've been trying to get better cost visibility across routes.
[00:12] Mark: yes, and we want concrete numbers for budgeting and a sense of latency tradeoffs.
[00:18] Carlos: great, i'll share my screen, i'll start in the console home — bear with me if the slide, uh the screen share takes a second.
[00:28] (screen share noise)
[00:32] Carlos: ok so this is the usage analytics page — top-left shows overall tokens in/out, token cost, and request counts over time. we surface median and p95 latency by route. you can filter by model, region, and by deployment type, so hosted vs dedicated.
[00:48] Anita: quick question — we have multiple routes: chat for customer support, summarization for internal docs, embeddings for search. how do you break out cost per route?
[00:55] Carlos: good question. each route is instrumented — so you see per-route token counts, average seq length, and effective token unit cost. the per-route dashboard over here shows token breakdown, and we also estimate CPU/GPU token-seconds for dedicated pods — that's how we derive a cost-per-token for committed capacity.
[01:18] Samantha: and importantly we tie that back to your billing partition so you can see which product line is eating budget.
[01:25] Mark: is the per-route cost real-time? like can i get last 24 hours?
[01:29] Carlos: yes, near real-time with a 1-5 minute lag for hosted. dedicated has an option to stream more granular metrics if you enable high-freq telemetry.
[01:38] Sarah: from procurement side we need a clear model — do you provide sample invoices or a cost model?
[01:44] Samantha: we'll send the pricing and a cost-model spreadsheet after this call, with examples mapped to a few usage profiles.
[01:50] Anita: can you show an example of optimizing a high-volume route? we've had big costs from our summarization route.
[01:55] Carlos: absolutely — i'll open the route view for "summarize-docs". here you can see request distribution, median tokens per request, and a suggestions panel. we recommend batching, KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes, and moving to a quantized variant for embeddings.
[02:12] Carlos: (mis-said) — the KV cash, uh K-V cache, sorry — sometimes the transcription spells it weird — but it's basically the token cache to avoid recomputing for repeated context.
[02:22] Mark: how much savings are we talking about?
[02:25] Carlos: typical wins depend on repetition — for high prefix reuse you can see 30-60% token reduction and 20-40% cost savings after quantization and batching; we'll tailor numbers in the spreadsheet.
[02:38] Anita: what's the impact on latency? we can't sacrifice p95 too much.
[02:42] Carlos: right — there's a tradeoff. batching improves throughput and unit cost but can increase tail latency if you wait to accumulate requests. our console shows expected latency delta for each optimization; you can set SLOs and the runtime will honor latency-first routing.
[02:56] Samantha: we also have automatic fallbacks to model variants and cross-region routing to keep availability up if a tier is constrained.
[03:05] Mark: can you show the cost breakdown by model family? we test a couple of open models.
[03:09] Carlos: yep — here's the model catalog view next to route: per-model perf profiles include tokens/sec, mem footprint, and cost index. you can simulate a route's cost under different model combos — that's the cost-simulator tool in the console.
[03:23] Anita: are the model perf numbers Redwood-verified?
[03:26] Carlos: they are benchmarked by our onboarding team and we include per-sequence-length profiles; still we recommend running a short benchmark with your workload — it'll show exact throughput and latency for your token distribution.
[03:38] Samantha: to be clear, we can provision a short dedicated pilot so you can run the benchmark with real traffic patterns.
[03:45] Mark: that would be ideal. also we need to know compliance posture — SOC 2 and SSO.
[03:51] Samantha: yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations. i'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:59] Sarah: procurement will need data residency and retention policies — can you confirm logs retention and ability to disable storage?
[04:06] Samantha: yes, retention is configurable and for private deployments you can opt for no retention and bring-your-own-key. we'll include those options in the security docs.
[04:14] Anita: on Dedicated — do we get reserved GPUs and predictable throughput?
[04:18] Carlos: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, autoscale rules, and isolation. the console shows committed throughput vs actual usage so you can tune policies and avoid overcommit charges.
[04:28] Mark: how do we estimate monthly cost for dedicated vs hosted?
[04:31] Carlos: the cost-simulator supports both modes. hosted is usage-based; dedicated is a committed monthly cost plus overage. we can build an org-specific estimate — which we'll include in the spreadsheet.
[04:42] (small cross talk)
[04:46] Samantha: let's run a quick demo of the per-route dashboard: i'll go to the 'routes' page and open 'customer-chat' — you can see token heatmaps, top prompts, and a contribution chart that maps token spend to features.
[04:59] Carlos: note the "cost attribution" feature — it tags each request with a feature label and shows cumulative spend for that label. this helps PMs see which features are most expensive.
[05:12] Anita: that's really useful. can we export this data? csv or direct to BI?
[05:16] Carlos: yes, export to CSV and there's a BI connector (we have a sample connector for BigQuery and Snowflake).
[05:23] Mark: any limitations on retention for the BI export?
[05:26] Carlos: export respects retention policy; if you need longer retention we offer add-on retention plans.
[05:31] Anita: okay, show me the cost breakdown widget.
[05:34] Carlos: here's the cost breakdown — top shows total token costs, then stacked by route and model. there's also a table with 'cost per 1k tokens' adjusted by model and quantization. you can click 'optimize' and the console will run scenarios recommending batching and model switches to hit a target cost or target p95 latency.
[05:55] Samantha: for the optimization suggestions we show estimated savings and a confidence level — this is driven by our telemetry plus model performance priors.
[06:05] Mark: do you surface recommendations for quantization levels? like 4-bit vs 8-bit?
[06:09] Carlos: yes we recommend quantization profiles and show expected regression risk in output quality; we link to evaluation testcases so product teams can verify.
[06:18] Anita: what's the rollback story if quality regresses?
[06:21] Carlos: rollouts are in the console — you can do canary, A/B, or instant rollback. and you can tie quality regression alerts to specific eval prompts so you'll be alerted if a metric dips.
[06:33] Samantha: ok quick diversion — any competitors you guys are looking at or evaluating?
[06:36] Anita: we've looked at OpenAI's hosted offering for dev speed and Anthropic in some tests; also we've seen smaller inference vendors.
[06:44] Samantha: cool — we have some notes comparing unit economics to OpenAI in the spreadsheet.
[06:48] Mark: one more technical — for our on-prem requirements, can Redwood run in our VPC?
[06:52] Carlos: yes, our Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem options; we have a private control plane and optional air-gapped package. performance characteristics are similar but you manage the hardware and network.
[07:04] Anita: what's needed from our side to start a dedicated pilot?
[07:07] Samantha: sample workload, expected QPS and token distribution, and a list of stakeholders. we'll provision a tenant and give access.
[07:14] Mark: timeline-wise we want procurement done in a couple weeks, ability to start a pilot end of month.
[07:19] Samantha: sounds doable — we'll send the pricing and the pilot provisioning checklist.
[07:24] (pause)
[07:26] Carlos: okay i'll jump into the benchmark tool briefly — you can upload a CSV of requests or use a traffic generator. it will run against a model and report throughput, p50/95 latencies, and GPU utilization.
[07:38] Carlos: note that for dedicated the tool can attach to a reserved pool and show consumed capacity vs reserved. for hosted we'll simulate under the hosted perf profile.
[07:48] Anita: do you support automatic KV caching for chat histories?
[07:52] Carlos: yes, we support prefix caching and application-level caching; you can enable K-V cache per route — reduces recompute for repeated context.
[07:59] Mark: any gotchas on cost attribution when you use caching?
[08:03] Carlos: cached responses reduce token usage so cost attribution will reflect lower token spend on that route; we also show cache hit-rate metrics.
[08:11] Samantha: okay let's note the agreed next steps.
[08:14] (brief recap)
[08:16] Samantha: action items: i'll send pricing + cost spreadsheet, carlos will prepare benchmark checklist, datawave will send sample workload, mark will confirm procurement timeline.
[08:26] Anita: thanks, and please include security pack.
[08:29] Samantha: yes. anything else?
[08:31] Sarah: procurement wants a draft contract template if possible.
[08:34] Samantha: we can share a standard SOW template, yes.
[08:36] Mark: can we also get a short video or export of the console walkthrough for our stakeholders?
[08:40] Carlos: i'll share a short recorded clip and the console export links.
[08:44] Samantha: great. we'll follow up with dates for the benchmarking session. thanks everyone.
[08:49] Anita: thanks, bye.
[08:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional minor transcription errors (K V cash, minor proper-name mis-hears). This is a sales/demo style walkthrough; tone is conversational and includes qualification, security questions, and explicit next steps.
